parts:
Hi Liz,

I'm not sure what that second line is doing -- it might just mean there was a change along the branch below node 168 -- is this a time-stratified analysis perhaps?  

Cheers!
Nick


On Fri, Sep 30, 2016 at 7:22 AM, <lizmil...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Nick,

Thank you so much for your assistance and attention to detail with your example scripts.

My goal is to use stochastic mapping to get a sample of states at nodes of my tree. So for my particular research problem, I am only interested in the states reconstructed at each node (less interested in types of dispersal/vicariance events and related information). 

I have started by looking at the cladogenic event table for one stochastic map simulation. I assumed (maybe incorrectly) that the cladogenic events would give me what I was looking for instead of the anagenic events table. However I am looking at the output:

node  node.type  time_bp  clado_event_type clado_event_txt  sampled_states_AT_nodes  sampled_states_AT_brbots
168  internal 49.87  vicariance (v) BCDH->BDH,C 189 208
168  internal 49.87 208 5
169  internal 39.59  vicariance (v) ACDEGH->H,ACDEG 420 83


So it appears that node 168 has two events associated with it. Assuming that the column "sampled_states_AT_nodes" contains a number corresponding to the reconstructed state, why would there be different numbers? (referring to the 189 and 208 associated with internal node 168). Again, all I want to know is which ancestral area was reconstructed at node 168 for this particular stochastic map. I have a tree with 166 taxa and 9 areas (max # areas = 9) with no null range.


Thank you again!
